subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - GPU type, reserved size, throughput targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@finlytics.com>, John Perez <john.perez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + follow-up: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification (GPU type, size, throughput)

Thanks again for taking the call today - great conversation. Below is a short recap and a few clarifying questions so we can lock down an accurate Dedicated quote.

Recap (what we heard)
- Expected monthly token usage (input + output): baseline ~1.2B tokens/month, peak scenario up to ~2.5B/month over the next 12 months.
- Typical request shape: avg context length ~512 tokens, avg output ~120 tokens (so average request ~632 tokens).
- Concurrency & SLA: application sees steady concurrency ~20-30 active requests, p95 latency target ~<400ms on synchronous calls.
- Budget guidance: you mentioned a target in the range of $700-600 per 1M tokens (you said $900/1M was a target to be competitive).
- Preference: Reserved dedicated capacity (predictable throughput + data isolation). Open to hybrid (reserved + hosted overflow) if it helps economics.

Clarifying questions (to confirm before we price):
1) Model family: which model family do you plan to serve? (e.g., Llama 2-70B quantized / RedMonarch-40B / similar). GPU selection and throughput assumptions change by model.
2) Effective cache hit rate: do you expect a lot of repeated prefixes or prompt templating? Even a modest KV/prefix cache (15-25%) materially reduces unit cost.
3) Commit length: are you looking at a 12-month reserved contract, 24-month, or pilot month to start?
4) Any strict networking or compliance requirements beyond what you shared (VPC peering, dedicated transit, custom KMS)?

Next steps from our side:
- Marcus (cc'd) will draft a ballpark dedicated configuration (GPU type + quantity) and back-of-envelope unit economics for your baseline and peak.
- If the numbers look good, we'll generate a formal quote (PDF) and propose a short POC: 2x H100 reserved for 30 days + hosted overflow to validate performance and assist with fine-tuning.

Attachment: finlytics_pricing_requirements.xlsx (Excel, 42 KB) - the sheet you shared; included here for quick reference.

Would you be able to confirm model family and commit length by end of week? Once we have that we'll send the draft pricing.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Recap + follow-up: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification (GPU type, size, throughput)

Hi Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and one follow-up ask below.

Answers:
- Model: primary workload will be an L2-70B quant (we plan to run a 4-bit quantized variant in prod). Secondary experiments with a 40B family for cheaper throughput.
- Cache: we expect ~20% effective prefix/KV cache on our most common flows (templates + customer metadata).
- Commit: we prefer a 12-month reserved commitment if the price makes sense. Pilot month is acceptable for validation but prefer to move to a 12-month after sign.
- Compliance: standard SOC2 + VPC peering should cover it; we may need certs for our procurement team later.

Budget/volume confirmation:
- Baseline: 1.2B tokens/month. Forecasted growth ~30% over 12 months (so plan for 1.6B in year +1).
- Peak: short bursts could approach 2.4-2.6B tokens/month during heavy campaigns.
- Target unit economics: our procurement target is $900 per 1M tokens (including all Redwood fees for dedicated).

One ask:
Can you provide a rough configuration that meets p95 <400ms for L2-70B quant with our concurrency (~25) and the 20% cache assumption? If that configuration maps to an 8-GPU pool (or similar), please include a ballpark committed monthly price and the implied $/1M tokens under your assumptions.

Attached: Finlytics_network_security_requirements.pdf (PDF, 75 KB) - procurement asked for this earlier.

Thanks,
Sarah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + follow-up: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification (GPU type, size, throughput) - internal notes

Internal - quick B.O.E. based on Sarah's answers (L2-70B quant, 1.2B baseline, 20% cache, 12-month commit desired). Numbers are rounded and include conservative headroom for bursts.

Assumptions:
- Model: L2-70B 4-bit quantized.
- Effective tokens/month to serve (after 20% cache reduction): baseline = 1.2B * 0.8 = 960M tokens/month.
- Average (compute-dominant) throughput per H100-equivalent GPU (sustained, with our optimized runtime): ~45M tokens/hour (~12.5k tokens/sec sustained) for this model under expected batch/concurrency mix. (This is a workload estimate; actual can vary by token length/beam/etc.)
- Operational reserve: add 20% headroom for spikes and autoscaling buffer.

Sizing (baseline):
- Tokens/hour (baseline): 960M / (24 * 30) = 444k tokens/hour.
- GPUs needed (baseline sustained): 444k / 45M = 0.01. this seems off because per-hour numbers - reframe by tokens/sec easier:
  - Baseline tokens/sec: 960M / (30*24*3600) = 370 tokens/sec.
  - H100-equivalent sustained tokens/sec: ~12,500 tokens/sec.
  - GPUs needed (baseline): 370 / 12,500 = 0.03 GPUs. indicates baseline is small vs GPU capacity.

Sizing (peak burst scenario):
- Peak month (2.4B tokens pre-cache = 1.92B after 20% cache): tokens/sec peak average across bursts could hit ~740 tokens/sec.
- To meet p95 <400ms under concurrency 25 and bursty traffic, target headroom ~3x average peak => design target ~2,200 tokens/sec.
- GPUs needed for headroom: 2,200 / 12,500 = 0.18. still <1 GPU, so H100 has plenty of headroom.

Conclusion / practical recommendation:
- For L2-70B quant, a small dedicated pool (2x H100) gives you predictable isolation, room for additional models, and headroom for spikes and future growth.
- Pricing back-of-envelope (example 12-month commit):
  - List: 2x H100 reserved pool equivalent pricing (internal list) = $85,000/month (example; exact depends on region & procurement).
  - Effective tokens/month (baseline): 960M -> implied price per 1M tokens = (85,000 / 960) = $88.5 / 1M tokens.

Notes on the math above: the derived $/1M looks extremely low because dedicated reserved hardware amortizes across very large token volumes - our baseline tokens are small relative to GPU capacity. The real cost to the vendor includes infra, overhead, and opportunity cost; our commercial pricing layers on top. Typical commercial dedicated pricing for this profile ends up in the $500-3,200 / 1M tokens band depending on discount and commitment.

Suggested commercial approach to meet Finlytics target ($900 / 1M):
- Offer 12-month commitment on 2x H100 with an effective commercial price ~ $900 / 1M tokens for the first 12 months (we can set a floor of committed monthly spend).
- Include a 30-day pilot (2x H100) priced pro-rata; if they convert to 12-mo commit within pilot, credit pilot fees.
- Hybrid fallback: allow hosted overflow for large marketing bursts (pay-as-you-go) so they don't over-provision reserved capacity.

I'll attach a draft quote PDF and the worksheet showing the full calculation. If legal wants a PO-style pricing sheet we can produce that next.

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_quote_v1.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

-Marcus

Proposed next steps:

2) If you want to target the $900/1M commercial goal, we can structure a 12-month commitment with that effective unit price for your baseline consumption band (with defined overage tiers for bursts). Marcus attached a draft quote.
3) Procurement check: I'll loop in legal/procurement once you confirm the 12-month preference and we'll share SOC2 + certs.
